## Standard Identifiers

| Identifier | Purpose | Generation |
|---|---|---|
| `anonymousId` | Tracks pre-login user activity; attached to anonymous users before authentication | **Client-side (auto-generated UUID)**; server-side (manual) |
| `userId` | Canonical identifier; attached when user authenticates (login, etc) | **Always manual** — generated on your backend/service |
| `groupId` | B2B relationships; identifies groups/accounts associated with users | **Always manual** — generated and maintained in your database |

## ID Format Recommendation

**Use `uuidv4` for all three identifiers.** Criteria:

| Trait | Why It Matters |
|---|---|
| **Global uniqueness** | Statistically unique without central coordination; ideal for distributed systems |
| **Non-sequential** | Harder to guess other valid IDs (security advantage vs incremental integers) |
| **No information leakage** | Doesn't encode creation time, personal data, or other metadata |
| **Standardized** | Widely recognized, supported across all platforms/languages |
| **No collision risk** | Infinitesimally small chance of duplicates even after billions generated |
| **Easy generation** | Available in virtually all programming languages |

## Persistence

**Client-side** (web/mobile):
- Libraries auto-store identifiers in cookies/localStorage (web) or device memory (mobile)
- IDs automatically fetched on subsequent requests
- Reset via `analytics.reset()` when user logs out or session ends

**Server-side**:
- No built-in persistence — you maintain IDs in your own database
- Rarely necessary — most servers process known users with existing `userId`
- If needed, deploy custom ID persistence on your infrastructure
